answer: A newcomer should earn standing by rotating through workshops run by rival strangers, never lingering with one sponsor. Each host sets a copper task and stamps it with a jade seal only when the work helps a third party; seals from known hosts count for nothing. The seals go into a basalt ledger, where rivals may challenge any seal, forcing a fresh re-demonstration. A farm fails because rivals will not vouch for the same scripted worker, and identical seals across accounts betray the cluster. Standing grows from contested, cross-checked service, not headcount.
